newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan stocks sag at close on selling pressure.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan stocks sag at close on selling pressure.

text.p: Pakistani stocks ended 1.41 percent down on Monday on selling pressure triggered on fears of a devaluation of Pakistani rupee against the dollar and dealers said the index would slip further.

But Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz told parlaiment later that now devaluation was planned at the moment, in apparent move to remove the fears sparked by his earlier on Thursday that hinted at the possibility of a marginal devaluation.
"Foreign and local investors and institutions all are on the sidelines," dealer Ali Asghar said. The Karachi Stock Exchange (KSE) 100-share index fell 22.47 points, to end at 1,568.83.
Losers beat gainers 225 to 52. Turnover rose to 45.48 million shares from 34.36 million in the previous session on Friday.
ICI Pakistan fell 0.60 to 24.20 rupees, PTCL 0.75 to 29.60 and Dewan Salman Fibre 0.85 to 38.60.
